segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As Jesus came over the hill and the whole city of Jerusalem opened up in front of him, he did something the crowds didn't expect.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He stopped. Luke writes it in one plain sentence:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: And when he was come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He came close, he looked at the city, and he cried over it. Not for himself. For them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The peace they had been aching for had walked right up to their gates — and the city was too busy to see it.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If only you had known — even you, even today — what would have brought you peace. But now it's hidden from your eyes. He is not scolding the city. He is talking to it the way you talk to someone you love who is about to walk past the one thing that would have saved them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He could see what was coming for the city he loved — armies and ruin, a generation away.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His tears weren't anger. They were the grief of love that sees exactly what could have been.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He wept because he loved the city that couldn't see him. He sees you clearly. Don't look away.
